    How to read this. Each investor's latest 13F is compared with their previous one. Est. $ flow = change in shares × the quarter-end price implied by the filing (so a position that was trimmed while its price rose still counts as selling). Conviction = that trade as a % of the investor's whole 13F portfolio, summed across investors. Position size before → after backs each position's weight out of the share counts at the filing's price, as a % of the larger of the investor's two quarterly portfolios. Market caps (bubble chart, company-size pyramid) come from the Yahoo Finance snapshot and are missing for some stocks — those are left out of those two charts only.

    Sold at a loss? 13F filings show holdings, not prices paid or profits. For the stock-pickers we rebuild each position from up to 10 years of their past 13Fs: shares bought in a quarter are costed at the midpoint of that quarter's start and end prices (average cost; splits detected), and a sale is compared the same way. "At a loss" means the sale was below the estimated cost even at the better of the two quarter-end prices. Positions older than the history we have are compared with the oldest price we have instead (◇). Estimates only — the real trade prices aren't public.

    13F filings are quarterly, due 45 days after quarter end, and show US-listed long positions only (no shorts; options excluded). Investors file on different days, so near a deadline some are a quarter behind — each one's quarter is shown above. Filers more than a quarter behind are marked stale and excluded. Prices in the company cards come from Yahoo Finance at the date shown. Not investment advice.
